title: Torus-knot trajectories have zero hyperbolic volume via Reeb
html:
Remark. Torus-knot trajectories have zero hyperbolic volume via Reeb

The 3-cycle braid words \sigma_1\sigma_2 and \sigma_2\sigma_1 rotate all three colour tubes uniformly with rate \dot\psi = \pm q. The trajectory traces a helix on a Heegaard torus T^2 \subset S^3. The trajectory completes a T_{2,3} torus knot (trefoil).

The complement of any torus knot admits a Seifert fibration. It supports no hyperbolic structure, meaning V_{\mathrm{hyp}}(T_{m,n}) = 0. The global-vortex flow maintains parallel strands, aligns with the Hopf fibre, and closes onto the Heegaard torus, guaranteeing a Seifert-fibered complement.

Consequently, the topological mass component of the Markov-trace observable vanishes for torus configurations. Torus knots yield zero hyperbolic volume, contributing only to the counting part of the trace.

The vanishing is corroborated at the level of quantum-invariant asymptotics. The colored Jones polynomials of a torus knot admit no volume-type limit: at the Kashaev point the growth is polynomial rather than exponential, and the deformed limit J_N(T_{m,n}; e^{2\pi i r/N}) degenerates to the inverse Alexander polynomial 1/\Delta(T_{m,n}; e^{2\pi i r}) for \mathrm{Im}\, r < 0 while producing a pure Chern–Simons phase for \mathrm{Im}\, r > 0, discontinuously across the real axis [murakami2004a]. No continuous volume-like potential exists for a torus knot; any mass carried by a torus-knot particle must therefore enter through a different chain than the volume route.
